newsitem.title: CHINA: China central bank mulls cutting reserve ratios.
newsitem.headline: China central bank mulls cutting reserve ratios.

text.p: China's central bank, the People's Bank of China, is considering cutting bank reserve ratios by 3.0 percentage points, the China news service quoted governor Dai Xianglong as saying recently.

The central bank requires commercial banks to keep reserves of 13 percent of deposits with another five to seven percent as separate provision funds. These funds are all held by the central bank, which pays 8.82 percent interest on them.
China would first reduce ratios for the 13 percent of deposits, the news service on Friday quoted experts as saying.

Only after the economic situation and financial environment had shown further significant improvement would the central bank move to unify the deposit reserves and the provision funds, it quoted the experts as saying.
The central bank would gradually reduce the ratio further, it said.
Dai was quoted earlier as saying that such a cut would not herald an easing of monetary policy, and said the central bank would recall loans extended to commercial banks after the ratio cut.
Overall money supply would not rise if the central bank recalled more loans from commercial banks than the amount of reserve it released, state media has said.
China has kept a tight rein on monetary policy since mid-1993 but cut interest rates on May 1 and has increased bank loans to selected state firms and key industries.
